page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, with 32.0 GB of system memory. The CPU includes a cache hierarchy of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers in the top 25% tier at 14.08 GB/sec. Most other compute benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average middle 50% range. However, the instance exhibits a weak performance profile in the Passmark CPU encryption test and poor prompt processing speeds for medium 7B LLM models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture and dedicated core allocation provide a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and high-speed local NVMe storage without the premium of specialized hardware. This makes the m8gd.2xlarge well-suited for general-purpose workloads, local database hosting, static web serving, and software compilation tasks that benefit from fast local storage and high memory bandwidth.
